newsitem.title: UK: India's Ranbaxy sees over 20 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: India's Ranbaxy sees over 20 pct growth.

text.p: Top Indian pharmaceutical company Ranbaxy Laboratories Ltd expects to show a growth of over 20 percent in the year to March 31, 1997, a company executive said on Wednesday.

"I think we are maintaining by and large the trend which we established in the first half. We should end the year with plus 20 percent (growth)," Ranbaxy's president Davinder Singh Brar told Reuters in an interview.
Ranbaxy, which earns half of its revenue from exports out of India, had reported a 20.6 percent rise in net profit for the six months to October 31, 1996 to 718 million rupees ($20 million).
The company, due to close its sales this week for 1996/97, would achieve net exports of five billion rupees, close to 47 percent of its turnover, Brar said.
Brar was in London to attend a global pharmaceuticals conference organised by the Financial Times.
British and U.S. financial institutions control about 17 percent in Ranbaxy after it issued global depositary receipts in 1994. ($ = 35.87 Indian Rupees)
